guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / minor wound care
title: Minor wounds at an inter-schools sports competition
setting: Inter-schools sports competition. A 10-year-old child collapsed with a cut knee and hand grazes after tripping over while running.
verdictExplanation: Alert, responsive, stable observations. A minor superficial cut on the knee and grazes with no systemic red flags. Not sick: simple wound care and safety-netting.

history.complaint: Cut on the knee from falling over
history.history: Tripped over while running, noticed broken metal on the ground where she fell
history.pmh: Has not had a tetanus immunisation
history.injuries: Small cut on knee, superficial grazes on palms, dirt inside wound
history.additional: Parents were not able to come to see her compete today

followUp.question: What is the correct management for this child's minor wounds?

options.text: Clean the knee and hands under cool water, dry, apply a sterile plaster, and advise parental review for tetanus
Call 999 immediately due to the risk of lockjaw (tetanus)
Apply a tourniquet above the knee to stop the minor bleeding
Leave the dirty wound open to air-dry and allow her to continue running the race

followUp.explanation: Minor wounds should be cleaned and dressed. Since she has dirt in the wound and has not had a tetanus immunisation, her parents must be advised to seek medical review. 999 is not indicated. Tourniquets are for life-threatening haemorrhage.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Wash wounds, dress. Inform school/parent regarding the dirt and tetanus status.
levelFlags.erNotes: Thoroughly clean wound (irrigate). Reassure, verify tetanus history, advise parents on infection signs.
